🧩 planning-shape: **one-off** — One card, one pull request. It owes no plan artifact and stops for no green light.

**Why:** Two independent monitor-rule fixes in one backend tier and one language (Python), each in its own file with its own replay test, which fits one pull request; the doubt is that it bundles two separately-caused defects, and the wip_health count must be pinned to the sweep's definition in another repo, so if the first monitor's root cause proves deep it hands back as two cards. — size tests checked: 1 contracts between the pieces, 2 two languages or two tiers, 5 specific is not small, 6 cut on file footprint, not only on concern

**Stamped by:** `planner` · **model:** `claude-fable-5-1`

**Where it goes:** Backlog. **Who handles it there:** reconcile.py.
🧠 model-attempt: claude-fable-5-1 (asked) / claude-fable-5-1 (answered) — planning classifier read the card.

🔁 **Pre-approval critic — before this is built** — sent back — round 1 of 2. Every finding here is a defect in the card an agent can fix, so the planner revises the card in place and the critic reads it again.

Reason: The last "done" test needs someone to watch the live console after release and quote the times on the card, which an unattended build cannot do, so it has to move out of the acceptance list.

Every finding this round (5), ranked — the revision answers all of them, and the next round checks those fixes rather than finding these again:

1. The last "done" test needs someone to watch the live console after release and quote the times on the card, which an unattended build cannot do, so it has to move out of the acceptance list.
2. The first test is to be built from "bureau-pipeline's real run list of 2026-10-10, recorded as a fixture", but the card never says how the builder gets that list. Those runs are in the production record and on GitHub, and the card itself says a build agent usually cannot read that repo's runs. Eith…
3. The "wording and bound" criterion says "last successful read" without saying what that means. This monitor reads fresh every pass, and the old row stays unchanged only because the monitor takes no action when it gets no answer. The card should say that is the case it means, so the builder does not …
4. The card says the cause of the first alert is "not determined", yet the first test must fail on today's code and name the cause in the PR. That is workable, because the cause is findable in the repository (see the working), but the card should say the cause is the builder's to find, not leave it op…
5. The second alert compares a count taken across all repositories against a cap that belongs to one repository (agent-bureau). The card says it has not checked what the sweep counts, but it is the heart of the fix, so the card should say the count must be for that one repository only.

This card is not going to the build queue yet, and nothing here is for the CEO — it stays in Planning while the planner rewrites it to answer every finding above, and the critic reads it again.

🔁 The planner revised this card in place to answer the critic. What it changed, finding by finding:

1. Moved the post-release observation out of the acceptance list into a closing section headed "After release (not an acceptance criterion)", written in the DRE-3075 deferred shape: the operator reads both rows after the release is live and records the PT times on this card, and the observation belongs on a follow-up card carrying `needs-human` and `no-code`, blocked by this one. The planner may not file cards in this run, so a person files that follow-up. The remaining criteria are all checkable against the diff and the tests.
2. Supplied the fixture on the card itself. I read bureau-pipeline's run list with the pipeline's own GitHub token at about 03:00 PT on 2026-10-10 and recorded it as a table: the newest completed run of each of the five watched names and of the five `self-` stubs the sweep itself names, with run id, number, conclusion, branch, start and update stamps, and the job count from the jobs endpoint. The card now says the builder transcribes that table into the test module and reads nothing from GitHub. The first criterion is rewritten to run over that fixture with the live alert's kind already open, so it proves the resolution rather than just the absence of a raise.
3. Defined "the last verdict" in the card's own words: the last tick on which every watched workflow answered and each was judged refused or normal, that is, the last tick that raised or resolved, or would have. The card states that the monitor reads fresh every tick, that it takes no action on a no-answer tick, and that this inaction is the one reason an old row stays unchanged, which is the case the rule is for. It says where to keep the time across ticks (the same store idiom the monitor already uses for lane state) and how to date a row raised before the change (from the dated sentence its body already carries). I also removed the "or stand down" option the original left open: standards/console-honesty.md rule 2 says unknown is shown as unknown, never as the last known value, and this monitor resolves only on positive evidence, so the alert carries its age and is never resolved on no answer. The bound stays the builder's to state, with a one-day recommendation and the reasons for it, and the 18-day test is unchanged.
4. Replaced "Not determined" with a section that gives the cause as read from the repository and says the builder confirms it against the fixture and the live Record and names it in the pull request. It has two halves. Half one: `WATCHED_WORKFLOWS` names the scaffold stubs, but in bureau-pipeline those filenames are the `workflow_call`-only reusables, so `agent-task.yml` there has only its five refused runs of 2026-09-09 and its newest completed run is a refusal forever, `qa-review.yml` has one refused run from June, and the other three have no runs at all. The sweep already resolves these names per repo (`build_workflow()` and its siblings in reconcile.py answer `self-agent-task.yml`, `pr-review.yml`, `self-agent-fix.yml`, `self-merge-gate.yml`). Half two: the body's "Read from GitHub at" wording predates the move of both reads onto the event Record, the body is refreshed on every raise whose content moved, so the last raising tick was 2026-09-22 11:31 PT, and every tick since has had no answer because the Record does not hold a window back to a run created on 2026-09-09. The fix for half one is a per-repo watch list, pinned against bureau-pipeline's own workflow directory, and that is now the second criterion.
5. Stated that the count is for the one repository whose cap the monitor reads (agent-bureau) and wrote out what the sweep's cap counts, read from where the sweep states it: `wip_base` keeps this repo's cards over the work-segment lanes with a stall window in the lane contract (Todo, In Progress, In Review today), drops epics and `automation` cards, and `counts_against_wip` drops cards carrying a person mark from the routing vocabulary, `no-code` cards and `PROOF:` cards. The card names why today's number is wrong (every routed card in every repo in `ACTIVE_STATES`, minus epics), says the body must name what it counted beside the cap, and rewrites the fourth criterion so the 30-card replay contains each kind of excluded card. The pin criterion now says what is compared to what: the console's lane set, excluded labels and proof prefix against bureau-pipeline's `config/lane-contract.json`, `config/routing-verdicts.json`, `linear_ops.NO_CODE_LABEL` and `dependabot_card.LABEL`, read from the `.bureau-pipeline/` checkout or fetched at `stable` under the two-copies rule, failing rather than skipping on a disagreement. The console cannot import reconcile.py, and the card says why, so the rule is held as data and pinned rather than restated as prose.

🔁 The critic reads the revised card again on the next planning run, which has been started — nothing here is for the CEO. If the revision still does not satisfy it, the card parks in Triage for the operator with every finding named.
